title: Angles and shapes
ks3: Geometry and measures: angle facts, parallel lines, polygons and properties of shapes
intro: Acute, obtuse and reflex angles, angle rules, parallel lines, polygons and the properties of 2D and 3D shapes.
description: Free KS3 Maths angles and shapes questions with answers: types of angle, angles on a line, round a point and in a triangle, parallel lines, polygons and properties of shapes. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9 (ages 9 to 14).

questions.q: What type of angle is 120°?
questions.hint: Is it more or less than 90°? More or less than 180°?
questions.explain: 120° is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.

questions.q: What do we call an angle that is less than 90°?
questions.hint: It is smaller than a right angle.
questions.explain: An angle less than 90° is acute. Between 90° and 180° is obtuse, and more than 180° is reflex.

questions.q: What type of angle is 250°?
questions.hint: Is it more than a straight line (180°)?
questions.explain: 250° is more than 180° but less than 360°, so it is a reflex angle.

questions.q: A clock shows exactly 3 o'clock. What type of angle do the two hands make?
questions.hint: The minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand points to 3. That is a quarter of the way round.
questions.explain: A quarter turn is 90°, so the hands make a right angle.

questions.q: The two angles are on a straight line. Find x.
questions.hint: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.

questions.q: Find the angle x in the triangle.
questions.hint: The angles in a triangle add up to 180°.

questions.q: Three angles meet at a point. Find y.
questions.hint: Angles round a point add up to 360°.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has two equal angles. The other angle is 40°. What size is each of the equal angles?
questions.hint: Take 40° from 180°, then share what is left equally.

questions.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are 90°, 85°, 110° and x. Find x.
questions.hint: The angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°.

questions.q: Two angles fit together to make a right angle. One of them is 35°. What is the other angle?
questions.hint: A right angle is 90°.

questions.q: A round pizza is cut into 8 equal slices from the centre. What is the angle at the point of each slice?
questions.hint: All the angles meet at the centre, so they add up to 360°.
questions.explain: The angles round a point add up to 360°, so each slice has 360° ÷ 8 = 45°.

questions.q: Two angles on a straight line are 2x° and 3x°. Find the value of x.
questions.hint: 2x + 3x must make 180.
questions.explain: 2x + 3x = 5x, and 5x = 180, so x = 180 ÷ 5 = 36. (The angles are 72° and 108°.)

questions.q: Two straight lines cross. The angles opposite each other (vertically opposite angles) are…
questions.hint: Draw an X and measure the angles opposite each other.
questions.explain: Vertically opposite angles are always equal.

questions.q: A line crosses two parallel lines. Alternate angles (making a Z shape) are…
questions.hint: Look for the Z shape.
questions.explain: Alternate angles are equal. Co-interior angles (a C or U shape) add up to 180°.

questions.q: A line crosses two parallel lines. One angle is 65°. What is the corresponding angle (making an F shape)?
questions.hint: Look for the F shape. Corresponding angles are in the same position at each crossing.
questions.explain: Corresponding angles are equal, so the angle is 65°.

questions.q: A line crosses two parallel lines. Two co-interior angles (making a C or U shape) are x and 110°. Find x.
questions.hint: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to 180°.

questions.q: The angles inside a hexagon add up to 720°. What is each angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.hint: A regular hexagon has 6 equal angles.

questions.q: What is the size of each exterior angle of a regular pentagon?
questions.hint: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°.
questions.explain: A pentagon has 5 sides, so each exterior angle is 360° ÷ 5 = 72°. (Each interior angle is 180° − 72° = 108°.)

questions.q: What do the interior angles of a pentagon add up to?
questions.hint: A pentagon can be split into 3 triangles from one corner. Each triangle has 180°.

questions.q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°. How many sides does it have?
questions.hint: Find the exterior angle first. Interior and exterior angles add up to 180°.
questions.explain: Each exterior angle is 180° − 150° = 30°. The exterior angles add up to 360°, so there are 360 ÷ 30 = 12 sides.

questions.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.hint: Think of a honeycomb cell.
questions.explain: A hexagon has 6 sides. A pentagon has 5 and an octagon has 8.

questions.q: Which shape has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
questions.hint: Squares, rhombuses and parallelograms all have two pairs.
questions.explain: A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides.

questions.q: Which triangle has all three sides the same length?
questions.hint: "Equi" means equal.
questions.explain: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three equal 60° angles. An isosceles triangle has two equal sides; a scalene triangle has none.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.hint: Don't forget the diagonals.
questions.explain: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: 1 across, 1 down and 2 along the diagonals.

questions.q: A shape has 4 equal sides, but its angles are not right angles. What is it?
questions.hint: It is like a square that has been pushed over.
questions.explain: A rhombus has 4 equal sides. If its angles were all 90° it would be a square.

questions.q: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
questions.hint: Count the edges of the two triangles, then the edges joining them.
questions.explain: Each triangle has 3 edges (6 in total), and 3 more edges join the triangles: 9 edges. (It has 6 vertices and 5 faces.)

questions.q: How many faces does a cube have?
questions.hint: Think of a dice. How many sides have spots on them?
questions.explain: A cube has 6 square faces. (It has 8 vertices and 12 edges.)

questions.q: Which quadrilateral has two pairs of equal sides next to each other and exactly one line of symmetry?
questions.hint: Think of the shape of a kite flying in the sky.
questions.explain: A kite has two pairs of equal adjacent sides and one line of symmetry. A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry and a square has 4; a parallelogram (that is not a rectangle or rhombus) has none.

questions.q: Count the faces (F), vertices (V) and edges (E) of a square-based pyramid. Work out F + V − E.
questions.hint: There is a square at the bottom and a point at the top. Count each carefully.
questions.explain: F = 5 (1 square and 4 triangles), V = 5 (4 at the bottom and 1 at the top), E = 8 (4 round the bottom and 4 up to the top). 5 + 5 − 8 = 2. (This is true for every shape like this: it is called Euler's formula.)
